A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IIPM/MMI study. Their text, equations, figures, experimental results, and Appendices A–D are readable and can be matched reliably despite reformatting.

before.justification: Section 6 and Figure 1 report original selective-classification experiments. Appendix C.1 and Figure 3 report an original correlation analysis on Wine.

after.justification: Section 6/Figure 1 and Appendix C.1/Figure 3 retain the study's original classification experiments and Wine correlation analysis.

M1.justification: The IIPM and MMI definitions, MMI-Lin bound, prediction procedure, and Appendix D estimator are unchanged. The altered total-variation identity in Remark 14 does not establish a revised computational method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate selective classification on Obesity, Digits, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, and correlations between uncertainty measures on Wine. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Entropy Difference and Generalised Hartley remain the comparison methods in the corresponding experiments. CIFAR-100 still compares MMI-Lin with Entropy Difference, without exact MMI or Generalised Hartley.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C retain accuracy–rejection curves/AUC, ten-predictor ensembles, centroid predictions, tabular train/test splits, and pretrained CIFAR models evaluated using ten test buckets. The Wine analysis still uses one train/test split.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 retains the same Wine pairwise-correlation analysis of MMI, MMI-Lin, Generalised Hartley, and Entropy Difference. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions state ten experimental repetitions and report means and standard deviations in Section 6/Figure 1. No new seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures appear.

E6.justification: Figures 1 and 3 retain their scores, curves, and correlations. For example, CIFAR-100 AUC remains 91.2±0.5 for MMI-Lin versus 90.3±0.6 for Entropy Difference, and the Wine MMI–Generalised Hartley correlation remains 0.98.

T1.justification: Remark 14 and its Appendix B.7 restatement change the singleton-difference sums by adding a factor of one-half and replacing absolute values with parentheses. This changes the mathematical assertion: the precise-probability expression becomes identically zero. The remaining theoretical statements and derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: extending IPMs to capacities, convergence and axiomatic results, MMI uncertainty measures, and a scalable upper bound validated through selective classification.

C2.justification: The interpretations of MMI–Generalised Hartley similarity and upper-bound tightness remain unchanged. Section 7 retains the same sampling-based estimation limitation and future directions concerning weaker theoretical conditions, computation, and regression.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 retains the hardware specification, ensemble construction, pretrained-model source, and evaluation instructions. The reproducibility-code repository link is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction adds Mohammadi et al.'s Shapley-attribution work, listed in both preprint and AAAI forms, and Caprio et al.'s work on fixed-point theorems for credal-set updates. The central novelty claims and comparison with prior metric frameworks remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 introduces numbered subheadings within Sections 2–4, updates affiliation/publication information, reorders the bibliography, and makes small wording edits. The overall narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Typography and citation colors change, retained figures are resized or repositioned, and Figure 2's boxes and label wrapping are adjusted. The same three figures and Appendix B.7 example table remain, without substantive display redesign.

improvement.justification: The heading and citation updates provide modest editorial benefits, but Remark 14 and Appendix B.7 worsen a localized mathematical error. v1 omitted the one-half normalization; v3 adds it while removing absolute values, producing a signed sum that is always zero for probability distributions. This reduces mathematical reliability while the core framework and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
